title: Unique coherent overlaps for finite etale covers at one normal level
statement: Let $V$ be a scheme, $A\to V$ a scheme over it, $U\subseteq V$ open, and $P\to U$ finite etale. For a finite family indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(s)$, let $B_j\to V$ be schemes, $W_j\subseteq V$ opens, $q_j:A\to B_j$ maps over $V$, and $Y_j\to B_j\times_VW_j$ finite etale covers. Fix specified identifications of their pullbacks to $B_j\times_V(W_j\cap U)$ with the pullback of $P$. Assume $A$ is locally Noetherian, quasi-compact, and normal: every stalk is an integrally closed domain. Assume the image of every generic point of every irreducible component of $A$ belongs to $U$. Then an overlap system [def-sfb-normal-tower-cover-gluing-data] exists. There is no covering assumption on the $W_j$, no common-level selection, and no assertion of a global cover. [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-irreducible-components]

proof.text: Put $A_U=A\times_V U$ and use the canonical transports of [def-sfb-normal-tower-cover-gluing-data]. Write $H_j=A\times_VW_j$, let $Z_j$ be the pullback of $Y_j$ along the chart map induced by $q_j$, and let $\theta_j$ be its transported identification over $U$. By [rem-pc-regular-normal](2), write $A$ as a finite disjoint union of open-and-closed normal integral components $C_a$. Any nonempty open $T\subseteq C_a$ is integral with the same integrally closed local rings and the same generic point $\eta_a$. Since $A_U$ contains $\eta_a$, the open $D=T\cap A_U$ is nonempty and integral with that generic point. Take $T=C_a\cap H_i\cap H_j$ when nonempty. All restrictions of $Z_i$ and $Z_j$ remain finite etale by the cited base-change stability results. The map $\delta_{ij}=\theta_j^{-1}\theta_i$ over $D$ gives a map between the generic restrictions of $Z_i|_T$ and $Z_j|_T$. Apply [lem-sbc-normal-integral-generic-hom-full] over $T$ to extend it uniquely to $a_{ij,a}:Z_i|_T\to Z_j|_T$. Apply the uniqueness clause of the same node over $D$: both $a_{ij,a}|_D$ and $\delta_{ij}$ have the given generic restriction, hence they agree. The component domains are pairwise disjoint opens covering $H_i\cap H_j$. Compose each $a_{ij,a}$ with $Z_j|_T\to Z_j|_{H_i\cap H_j}$ and apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to glue these maps to $\alpha_{ij}$; their equations over the base glue as well. If the overlap is empty there is its unique empty-domain map.

proof.text: On any nonempty $C_a\cap H_i\cap H_j$, two maps between the indicated finite etale covers agreeing on $A_U$ agree at $\eta_a$, hence are equal by [lem-sbc-normal-integral-generic-hom-full]. The same statement holds on triple intersections, since they too are opens of $C_a$ containing $\eta_a$ whenever nonempty. Thus the constructed $\alpha_{ij}$ is the unique extension of $\delta_{ij}$. Over $A_U$ one has $\delta_{ji}\delta_{ij}=\mathrm{id}$, $\delta_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $\delta_{jk}\delta_{ij}=\delta_{ik}$ by cancellation of the specified $\theta$'s. Generic uniqueness gives these identities on each component of the corresponding overlap, and equality on this open cover gives equality globally by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. In particular $\alpha_{ji}$ is inverse to $\alpha_{ij}$, and all the required identity and cocycle conditions hold.
